extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2022 reviewers (peer reviewers for a machine-learning conference)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and expectations for reviewers evaluating submissions to ICLR 2022, including procedural deadlines, review content/structure, ethical obligations, discussion behavior, and how to form final recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write reviews within the conference deadlines; be thorough so SACs/ACs/PCs can rely on them for decisions. Timeliness is emphasized in the main reviewer tasks and schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to reviewing guidelines, Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: You follow the reviewing guidelines below and adhere to our Code of Ethics in your role as a reviewer. You must also adhere to our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag potential CoE violations and report them via the CoE report; contact AC/PC/ethics board as appropriate for resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reviewer onboarding tasks (profile & DBLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create your OpenReview profile and link your DBLP profile (by September 15th 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping profile metadata updated helps conflict-of-interest detection and assignment quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid on papers within bidding window
rubrics_metrics.description: Bid on papers (7 October 2021 - 12 October 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bidding to express expertise/interest and to avoid conflicts; update bids carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write constructive, thorough, timely review
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a constructive, thorough and timely review (14 October 2021 - 1 November 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize reviews to be useful to area chairs and authors; be detailed and specific rather than brief judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in discussion phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss with authors, other reviewers, and ACs to clarify and improve the paper (9 November 2021 - 29 November 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be actively engaged and responsive during the discussion phase; respond to comments/requests within 3 business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide final recommendation by deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a final recommendation to the area chair assigned to the paper (by 29 November 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update your review considering discussion and any author revisions; be open to changing your initial recommendation either more positive or negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag potential Code of Ethics (CoE) violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag any potential CoE violations and/or concerns (throughout the review and discussion phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate CoE violations when submitting the CoE report for that paper. AC will work with PC and ethics board. For other policy violations (plagiarism, double submission, paper length, formatting), contact AC or PC as appropriate via official comment with readership restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful reading and background checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the paper: It’s important to carefully read through the entire paper, and to look up any related work and citations that will help you comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time for this step; consult supplementary material if needed (not required but can answer questions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the objective of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: While reading, consider: What is the goal of the paper? (address a known application/problem, draw attention to a new application/problem, introduce/explain a new theoretical finding, or a combination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations as to potential value and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate strong points (clarity, correctness, rigor, reproducibility, novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong points: is the submission clear, technically correct, experimentally rigorous, reproducible, does it present novel findings (e.g. theoretically, algorithmically, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and explain these pros in the review; cite evidence such as experiments or proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate weak points
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak points: is it weak in any of the aspects listed in strong points (clarity, correctness, rigor, reproducibility, novelty)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as comprehensive as possible in listing cons and what would be needed to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of bias and be open-minded
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of potential biases and try to be open-minded about the value and interest a paper can hold for the entire ICLR community, even if it may not be very interesting for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting personal tastes determine accept/reject; consider broader community value and longer-term impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three key evaluation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer three key questions to form a recommendation: (1) What is the specific question/problem tackled? (2) Is the approach well motivated and well-placed in the literature? (3) Does the paper support the claims (results are correct and scientifically rigorous)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to decide accept vs reject and to explain your reasoning to ACs and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure: summary of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize what the paper claims to contribute. Be positive and generous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear concise summary helps ACs and authors understand your reading of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure: list strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: List strong and weak points of the paper. Be as comprehensive as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize pros/cons clearly; prioritize the most important issues for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure: state clear recommendation with reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state your recommendation (accept or reject) with one or two key reasons for this choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State concise core rationale up front; expand with supporting arguments later in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting arguments for recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supporting arguments for your recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evidence from experiments, theory, related work comparisons; quantify issues when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask focused questions to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask questions you would like answered by the authors to help you clarify your understanding and provide the additional evidence you need to be confident in your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions should be targeted and help authors address the review's main concerns during rebuttal/revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide additional feedback aimed to improve the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional feedback with the aim to improve the paper. Make it clear that these points are here to help, and not necessarily part of your decision assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate improvement suggestions from decision-critical issues; be constructive and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be polite and imagine being the recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite in your review. Ask yourself whether you’d be happy to receive a review like the one you wrote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone matters—'criticising with kindness' is recommended; avoid derogatory or dismissive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be precise, concrete, and cite references for claims about prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Be precise and concrete. For example, include references to back up any claims, especially claims about novelty and prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting related-work omissions or novelty, point to specific papers and explain differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly state uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s fine to explicitly state where you are uncertain and what you don’t quite understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may be able to resolve uncertainties in the response; clarifying uncertainty helps ACs weight your confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject solely for lack of 'interest'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t reject a paper just because you don’t find it 'interesting'. This should not be a criterion at all for accepting/rejecting a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider community value even if the paper isn't appealing to you personally; long-term or niche value can still merit acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material handling
rubrics_metrics.description: How should I use supplementary material? It is not necessary to read supplementary material but such material can often answer questions that arise while reading the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reviewing supplementary material before asking authors questions that it already addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling policy violations and contacting leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: To flag CoE violations indicate them in the CoE report. To discuss other violations (plagiarism, double submission, paper length, formatting), contact either the AC or the PC as appropriate via an official comment with the appropriate readership restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified channels (OpenReview official comments) and add appropriate readers when contacting ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact the Area Chair
rubrics_metrics.description: To contact the AC for a paper: go to the OpenReview page (while logged in); click the button to add an official comment and fill out the comment form; add the ACs to the list of 'Readers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use official comment mechanism rather than private messages for record and correct readership control.

rubrics_metrics.name: When asking for additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for additional experiments, but make sure you justify why they’re necessary to push the paper over the acceptance threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New experiments should not significantly change the submission's content; they should be limited in scope and serve to more thoroughly validate existing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art performance is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission does not achieve state-of-the-art results, this is not by itself grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions bring value when they convincingly demonstrate new, relevant, impactful, or insightful knowledge even without SOTA numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for citing recent/ArXiv work
rubrics_metrics.description: We consider papers contemporaneous if published (available in online proceedings) within the last four months; authors are not required to compare to such very recent papers. Authors may be excused for not knowing about papers not published in peer-reviewed proceedings or journals (including arXiv-only papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should use good judgment and discuss with the area chair if in doubt about required comparisons to very recent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding and reporting conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: How can I avoid being assigned papers that present a conflict of interest? Conflicts are detected using your OpenReview profile (co-authors, past/current institutions, etc.). Update your OpenReview profile. If you find a paper presenting a conflict when bidding, bid 'Very Low'. If assigned a paper that presents a conflict, contact the program chairs immediately to have it re-assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep profile metadata current; use bidding to flag conflicts and contact chairs promptly if misassignments occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear, well-structured example reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow examples of well-structured reviews (summaries, pros/cons, concrete questions, typos/minor comments separated) as models for formatting and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide provides an 'Accept' and 'Reject' example that show clarity, comprehensiveness, prioritized concerns, and polite tone.
